Jordan / team,

High-level from Finance: we cannot fully delete invoice records that are required for revenue recognition, tax reporting, and audit traceability. Accounting rules and our own retention obligations (US GAAP / local tax regs) require we preserve an immutable copy of invoices and the ledger entries for at least the statutory period (typically 7 years in many jurisdictions).

That said, there are practical approaches to meet both parties halfway:
- Preserve an immutable ledger and original invoice artifacts in an access-restricted, tamper-evident archive (audit-only).
- Provide the customer with redacted copies of invoice PDFs where PII (billing contact emails, personal phone numbers) is removed.
- Where invoices are purely corporate (company-level billing IDs), we can keep and surface them because they're necessary to substantiate revenues.

Operational notes and timeline:
- I can generate an "Audit Extract" CSV (invoice numbers, dates, net amounts, tax amounts) with only company identifiers (no billing contact) within 3 business days after we receive their ID list.
- Producing redacted invoice PDFs will take longer (5–7 business days) depending on volume; we'll run a batch redaction job that stamps "redacted per DSAR".

Please confirm if legal wants a formal hold letter or if we should respond directly to Maple with the above proposal.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Finance Operations
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: Audit_evidence_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Data erasure request (invoices + usage) -- need guidance

Team,

Agree with Neha's summary. A few legal points to be explicit about when we reply to Maple Health:
1) Legal hold vs. DSAR: statutory/regulatory obligations (tax, accounting, litigation) create lawful bases for preserving certain records even when a DSAR requests erasure. We should reference that we will preserve accounting records to meet legal obligations and provide a narrow, redacted export for the customer's purposes.
2) Scope and minimization: confirm exactly which identifiers Maple wants removed. Achieving full erasure of all traces across backups and immutable ledgers is not always possible or legally permissible. We should offer the redacted audit extract plus redacted invoice PDFs and document the retention rationale.
3) Formal notice: propose sending Maple a clear response that (a) acknowledges the DSAR, (b) explains the legal basis for preserving accounting records, (c) offers redacted deliverables, and (d) provides contact for escalation or a review by their Data Protection Officer.
4) Records we will preserve: invoice images, transaction-level ledger entries, tax reports, and internal reconciliation logs. Access to those will be logged and restricted to audit/finance/legal.

Action items for reply draft: Neha to prepare the audit extract + redaction estimate; Marissa to confirm which invoice storage buckets are on immutable retention and whether we can create a customer-scoped export without exposing other customers; Soojin to confirm there are no security concerns around the export process (S3 presigned URL vs. secure transfer). I can draft the legal language for the customer-facing email once we have the numbers.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data erasure request (invoices + usage) — proposed path forward

Hi Elaine (and Finance team),

Thanks for the DSAR and the prompt CSV — appreciate the detail. Quick summary and proposed path forward from Redwood:

1) What we will preserve: immutable copies of invoices, ledger entries, and tax reports necessary for statutory recordkeeping and audit. These are retained in our finance archive for compliance and cannot be fully deleted.

2) What we will provide to Maple Health: a) an Audit Extract CSV containing invoice number, invoice date, company billing ID, amount, and tax amounts (no billing contact PII); b) redacted invoice PDFs where billing contact emails and personal phone numbers are removed/stamped; c) a short attestation documenting the legal basis for preservation.

3) Timeline: upon receipt of the final ID list we will: i) produce the Audit Extract within 3 business days; ii) provide an estimate and schedule for redacted PDFs within 48 hours after that; iii) deliver redacted PDFs in batches (5–7 business days depending on volume).

4) Security & transfer: we will share exports via an access-controlled Drive folder and provide an audit log of downloads. If you prefer an encrypted SFTP transfer, we can arrange that instead.

5) Next step: please confirm you accept the above approach (preserve immutable accounting records while receiving redacted copies). If acceptable, we'll send a formal response letter (including legal rationale) and a HubSpot/DocuSign acknowledgement of the DSAR for your records.

If you want to discuss on a quick call, I'm available tomorrow 10am–12pm PT.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
